faq.q: Why do particles move by themselves?
faq.a: All particles have energy and are always moving. In a gas they move fast and freely, bumping into each other and changing direction all the time.
It is a difference in how crowded particles are between two places. Particles diffuse down the gradient, from where there are many to where there are few.
Diffusion is the net spreading of particles from an area of high concentration to an area of low concentration, caused by their random movement. It needs no energy from a cell.

faq.q: Does diffusion happen faster when it is hot?
faq.a: Yes. Higher temperature gives particles more energy, so they move faster and spread out more quickly. A steeper concentration gradient and a shorter distance also make it faster.
asks: Tell me about warmer is faster

faq.q: Where does diffusion happen in my body?
faq.a: Oxygen diffuses from your lungs into your blood, carbon dioxide diffuses the other way, and digested food diffuses from your gut into your blood.
asks: Does diffusion happen in the lungs?

facts: Diffusion is the net movement of particles from high to low concentration and needs no energy from cells.
Oxygen enters the blood in the alveoli of the lungs by diffusion.

quiz.say: Perfume spreads faster in a warm room. Why?
quiz.show: Perfume spreads faster in a warm room. Why?
quiz.why: Heat gives particles more energy, so they move and spread faster.

wrong.0: Even in still air, the speed-up comes from faster-moving particles, not pushing.
wrong.2: Being heavier would not make it spread faster.

quiz.say: In diffusion, particles move overall from…
quiz.show: In diffusion, particles move overall from…
quiz.why: Random motion makes particles spread from crowded places to less crowded ones.

wrong.0: Moving from low to high needs energy; that is active transport.
wrong.2: Diffusion happens in every direction, not only up.
